record.paper_title: Open problems in Gaussian fluid queueing theory
record.original_question: Develop a reliable and efficient simulation algorithm for estimating the generalized Pickands constant H_η. The method should avoid the instability of straightforward Monte Carlo schemes based directly on the defining representation of H_η(T)/T and should work for the class of Gaussian processes η considered in the paper.

evidence.quote: This explains why the methods needed cannot be straightforward, crude Monte Carlo type of procedures.
Open Problem 4.2 Develop a reliable simulation algorithm for efficient estimation of Hη.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let η = {η(t) : t ≥ 0} be a centered Gaussian process with stationary increments, almost surely continuous sample paths, η(0) = 0, and variance function σ²_η(t) = Var η(t) that is regularly varying at infinity with index in (0, 2). For T > 0, define
   H_η(T) = E[ exp( sup_{t ∈ [0,T]} ( η(t) − σ²_η(t)/2 ) ) ].
It is known that the limit
   H_η = lim_{T → ∞} H_η(T)/T
exists in (0, ∞); this is the generalized Pickands constant associated with η.

The problem is to construct a provably reliable and computationally efficient simulation (Monte Carlo) algorithm that produces consistent estimates of H_η with quantifiable error (bias and variance) for the whole class of admissible Gaussian processes η described above. The algorithm should avoid the instability of naive Monte Carlo schemes based directly on the ratio H_η(T)/T (whose variance blows up as T grows, while bias decreases), and should come with rigorous error bounds and a clear prescription for choosing its tuning parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: Dieker and Yakir (Bernoulli, 2014) introduced a representation of Pickands' constants as a plain expectation (no limit), yielding a reliable Monte Carlo estimator with explicit error analysis for the classical fractional-Brownian-motion Pickands constants H_α. This work is widely regarded as resolving the simulation problem in the classical case, and subsequent papers (e.g. on speed of convergence of discrete to continuous Pickands constants, and generalized/Berman-type extensions) have extended the methodology. A fully general, uniformly reliable simulation scheme covering all generalized Pickands constants H_η for arbitrary admissible Gaussian processes η is not established in a single definitive reference, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On asymptotic constants in the theory of extremes for Gaussian processes (Dieker–Yakir)
status_evidence.snippet: New representation of Pickands' constants as an expectation, enabling Monte Carlo estimation with detailed error analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a reliable simulation method for classical Pickands constants, partially solving the open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the speed of convergence of discrete Pickands constants to continuous ones
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes the discretization error of Pickands-constant estimators of Dieker–Yakir type.
status_evidence.claim: Extends and quantifies error of Dieker–Yakir simulation approach.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Pickands constants and stationary max-stable processes
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized Pickands constants associated with classes of Gaussian and max-stable processes.
status_evidence.claim: Provides representations applicable to generalized Pickands constants, supporting simulation extensions.
